articles.title: Justiça suspende venda de gasolina a preço de custo em Florianópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida valia para 20 estabelecimentos. Procon afirmou que vai recorrer.
articles.summary: Procon afirmou que vai recorrer.
articles.body:
Bomba em posto de combustível — Foto: Divulgação

A Justiça suspendeu temporariamente, com uma decisão liminar, a medida determinada pelo Procon de Florianópolis para 20 postos de combustíveis da cidade venderam a gasolina a preço de custo . A ação seria feita neste sábado (14).

A decisão judicial foi divulgada pelo próprio Procon na noite desta quinta (12). O órgão afirmou que vai recorrer.

O Procon de Florianópolis informou que respeita a decisão judicial e apresentará os esclarecimentos necessários, defendendo a legalidade da atuação e a manutenção da medida adotada.

Por que os postos venderiam a gasolina a preço de custo?

A venda de gasolina a preço de custo ocorreria neste sábado em 20 postos de combustíveis de Florianópolis das 7h às 15h, ou até que acabasse o limite de 7 mil litros estipulado para cada estabelecimento.

Com a medida, o custo do litro de gasolina ficaria entre R$ 5,28 e R$ 5,45.

A determinação do órgão municipal seria resultado de uma fiscalização do Procon dos preços dos combustíveis, que comparou os valores de aquisição da gasolina comum com os preços praticados na revenda e verificou que a redução no custo feita a nível federal não se refletiu no preço do litro na bomba.

A venda a preço de custo buscaria levar esse benefício diretamente ao consumidor que fosse abastecer o veículo.

O Procon Florianópolis disse que seguirá fiscalizando os postos de combustíveis e poderá exigir notas fiscais de aquisição, documentos de formação dos preços e demais informações necessárias para verificar possíveis aumentos injustificados ou práticas abusivas.

articles.title: VÍDEO mostra transatlântico histórico afundando na costa da Flórida | G1
articles.standfirst: O projeto, orçado em cerca de US$ 13,5 milhões, busca atrair mergulhadores e entusiastas da pesca para a região.
articles.summary: O projeto, orçado em cerca de US$ 13,5 milhões, busca atrair mergulhadores e entusiastas da pesca para a região.
articles.body:
Um vídeo divulgado por autoridades da Flórida mostra o momento em que um transatlântico histórico foi afundado, na quarta-feira (11), nas águas do Golfo do México, a aproximadamente 40 km de Destin, na costa dos Estados Unidos.

O objetivo é transformar a embarcação no "maior recife artificial do mundo" e em um destino turístico.

Maior que o Titanic, o transatlântico SS United States realizou mais de 800 viagens nas décadas de 1950 e 1960. Seu casco tem mais de 300 metros de comprimento — cerca de 30 metros a mais que o Titanic.

Foto de arquivo: o transatlântico aposentado SS United States em um cais na Filadélfia, Pensilvânia, em 10 de outubro de 2015. — Foto: Jewel Samad/AFP

Para que o navio afundasse sem o uso de explosivos, foram abertas as válvulas que alimentavam seu sistema de refrigeração, mais de 400 vigias do casco foram removidas e grandes aberturas foram feitas em seus conveses.

O projeto, orçado em cerca de US$ 13,5 milhões, busca atrair mergulhadores e entusiastas da pesca para a região do recife artificial, anunciado como o maior do mundo, que criará um habitat para a fauna marinha.

Equipes se preparam para afundar o antigo transatlântico SS United States para criar um recife artificial a cerca de 35 km da costa de Destin, Flórida, EUA, em 11 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Tony Giberson/USA Today Network via Reuters

O imponente transatlântico transportou a bordo inúmeras celebridades, entre elas John F. Kennedy, Marilyn Monroe, Salvador Dalí e até mesmo Walt Disney. Bill Clinton também viajou no navio durante sua juventude, quando se dirigia à Universidade de Oxford para estudar.

A primeira travessia do Atlântico pelo SS United States ocorreu em 1952, e a última, em 1969.

Agora, a gigantesca embarcação deverá repousar no fundo do mar, a 55 metros de profundidade, com seu ponto mais alto a 18 metros da superfície.

Até agora, o maior recife artificial era um antigo porta-aviões afundado há vinte anos na costa de Pensacola, também na Flórida.

Antes de ser transformado em recife submarino, o SS United States passou mais de um quarto de século atracado em um cais da Filadélfia, na costa leste dos Estados Unidos.

Transatlântico histórico é afundado na costa da Flórida — Foto: Destin-Fort Walton Beach via Reuters

articles.title: Acidente entre carro e moto deixa dois feridos em Valença | G1

articles.body:
Acidente entre carro e moto deixa dois feridos em Valença — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Dois homens ficaram feridos após um acidente entre um carro e uma moto na tarde desta quinta-feira (12) em Valença (RJ). O caso aconteceu no bairro João Dias.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o acionamento aconteceu às 13h20 para o atendimento na Rua 27 de Novembro.

Ainda de acordo com a corporação, os dois feridos foram atendidos por uma ambulância do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU) e foram encaminhados para o Hospital Escola de Valença.

O g1 entrou em contato com a unidade médica para atualizar o estado de saúde dos feridos, mas não obteve retorno.

Até o momento da publicação desta reportagem, a dinâmica do acidente era desconhecida.

articles.title: Ministério da Saúde abre concurso com salários de até R$ 10,3 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Processo seletivo aceita profissionais de diferentes formações superiores. Inscrições vão até 14 de dezembro, com taxa de R$ 60 e provas em janeiro.
articles.summary: Processo seletivo aceita profissionais de diferentes formações superiores. Inscrições vão até 14 de dezembro, com taxa de R$ 60 e provas em janeiro.
articles.body:
Sede do Ministério da Saúde em Brasília — Foto: Rodrigo Coutinho/MS

O Ministério da Saúde publicou nesta quinta-feira (12) o edital de um processo seletivo simplificado para contratar profissionais de nível superior em seis áreas. São 300 vagas para contratação imediata e outras 459 destinadas ao cadastro de reserva.

As remunerações iniciais variam de R$ 4.740,51 a R$ 10.354,29 , com auxílio-alimentação de R$ 1.192.

As inscrições começam nesta quinta-feira (12) e seguem até 14 de dezembro, exclusivamente pela internet, no site do Instituto Avalia. A taxa é de R$ 60.

O edital prevê isenção total da taxa para candidatos inscritos no Cadastro Único para Programas Sociais do Governo Federal (CadÚnico) que atendam aos critérios de baixa renda, pessoas de famílias com renda mensal de até meio salário mínimo por pessoa e doadores de medula óssea em entidades reconhecidas pelo Ministério da Saúde.

O processo seletivo foi aberto pela Secretaria-Executiva do Ministério da Saúde para atender a uma necessidade temporária de excepcional interesse público. Os contratos terão duração inicial de um ano , com possibilidade de prorrogação, caso seja necessário mais tempo para concluir as atividades previstas.

Todas as oportunidades exigem formação de nível superior, mas os requisitos variam conforme o cargo.

Há vagas para profissionais formados em qualquer área e outras destinadas a candidatos com graduação em cursos específicos, como Administração, Direito, Economia, Enfermagem, Medicina, Engenharia e Arquitetura.

A jornada de trabalho será de 40 horas semanais , em regime presencial . Os profissionais selecionados poderão atuar em Brasília (DF), Belém (PA), Belo Horizonte (MG), Curitiba (PR), Goiânia (GO), Recife (PE) e São Paulo (SP).

Ministério da Saúde abre processo seletivo com 300 vagas imediatas e 459 para cadastro de reserva. — Foto: Arte/g1

A seleção será organizada pelo Instituto Avalia e terá prova objetiva e avaliação de títulos e experiência profissional.

A prova objetiva será eliminatória e classificatória. Já a avaliação de títulos e experiência profissional terá caráter apenas classificatório e poderá acrescentar até 20 pontos à nota final.

Para os cargos de técnico administrativo e analista, a prova objetiva terá 40 questões. Já para o cargo de gestor, serão 50 questões.

Todas as questões terão cinco alternativas, com apenas uma resposta correta. A prova será aplicada na tarde de 17 de janeiro de 2027 e terá duração de quatro horas.

Para não ser eliminado, o candidato deverá obter pelo menos 50% da pontuação total da prova e não poderá zerar nenhuma área de conhecimento.

A classificação final será definida pela soma das notas da prova objetiva e da avaliação de títulos e experiência profissional.

Quais são os requisitos para assumir a vaga?

Além de comprovar a formação exigida para o cargo, o candidato deverá cumprir as demais condições previstas no edital no momento da contratação.

Entre elas estão ter pelo menos 18 anos, estar em dia com as obrigações eleitorais e militares, quando aplicável, estar no pleno exercício dos direitos políticos e ter aptidão física e mental para exercer as funções.

O candidato também não poderá ter sido contratado com base na Lei nº 8.745/1993 nos últimos 24 meses, salvo nas situações previstas como exceção pela legislação.

A documentação que comprova a formação e o cumprimento das demais exigências deverá ser apresentada no momento da contratação.

12 de novembro de 2026: publicação do edital e início das inscrições e dos pedidos de isenção.

16 de novembro: prazo final para solicitar isenção da taxa.

25 de novembro: divulgação do resultado dos pedidos de isenção.

4 de dezembro: divulgação do resultado dos recursos sobre a isenção.

14 de dezembro: encerramento das inscrições.

15 de dezembro: prazo final para pagamento da taxa e envio de documentos.

4 de janeiro de 2027: divulgação do resultado definitivo das inscrições.

7 de janeiro: divulgação dos locais de prova.

17 de janeiro: aplicação da prova objetiva.

18 de janeiro: divulgação do gabarito preliminar.

2 de fevereiro: divulgação do resultado preliminar da prova objetiva.

10 de fevereiro: divulgação do resultado definitivo da prova objetiva.

14 e 15 de fevereiro: realização dos procedimentos de heteroidentificação.

10 de março: divulgação do resultado preliminar da avaliação de títulos e experiência profissional.

19 de março: divulgação do resultado da avaliação de títulos e da classificação preliminar.

30 de março: divulgação do resultado final e homologação do processo seletivo.

articles.title: Trump diz que quer 'resolver a questão de Cuba' antes de deixar cargo | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos Estados Unidos afirmou que poderia usar a força para derrubar o governo da ilha e que o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, tem interesse em atuar na região.
articles.summary: Presidente dos Estados Unidos afirmou que poderia usar a força para derrubar o governo da ilha e que o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, tem interesse em atuar na região.
articles.body:
O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, gesticula enquanto o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com a imprensa no dia da cúpula de líderes da OTAN em Ancara, Turquia, em 8 de julho de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Umit Bektas

O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , afirmou nesta quinta-feira (12) que considera usar força contra Cuba . A declaração foi feita durante uma entrevista ao canal de TV americano "Salem News Channel", ao ser questionado se ordenaria uma operação militar para derrubar o governo do país.

"Eu certamente consideraria isso, sim", respondeu Trump.

O republicano também disse que acompanha de perto a situação na ilha, que classificou como uma nação falida. Ele mencionou o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio , filho de imigrantes cubanos, e afirmou que o chefe da diplomacia americana gostaria de atuar para mudar a situação do país.

Trump também citou o apoio recebido de eleitores cubano-americanos nas últimas eleições. Segundo ele, sua aporvação entre o eleitorado latino da Flórida vem aumetando desde 2024, quando ele foi eleito para seu segundo mandato.

"Francamente, eu gostaria de poder fazer isso para as pessoas, para os cubanos que vieram. Foram muito maltratados [em Cuba] e vieram para os Estados Unidos".

Não é a primeira vez que Trump ameaça intervir na ilha de Cuba. No final de outubro, o republicano afirmou que os Estados Unidos cuidariam de Cuba depois de lidarem com o Irã e que enviariam o secretário de Estado Marco Rubio para finalizar o acordo.

O governo Trump já havia declarado anteriormente que seu objetivo é mudar o governo comunista de Cuba.

O agravamento das tensões entre Washington e Havana ocorre em meio a uma grave crise econômica e energética em Cuba. Em 2026, o país enfrentou sucessivos apagões nacionais, que deixaram milhões de pessoas sem eletricidade.

A situação foi agravada pela escassez de combustível e pela deterioração da infraestrutura elétrica, com usinas termelétricas antigas e problemas frequentes de manutenção.

A crise se intensificou depois que os Estados Unidos interromperam o fornecimento de petróleo venezuelano à ilha, após a captura do presidente Nicolás Maduro, em janeiro de 2026. A Venezuela era o principal fornecedor de combustível de Cuba.

articles.title: Chefe da Nvidia pede demissão em meio a escândalo de espionagem e a revelação de novos casos extraconjugais | G1
articles.standfirst: Para muitos, Jensen Huang era o executivo mais poderoso do mundo. Ele liderava a empresa que controla cerca de 90% do mercado de chips avançados, usados na inteligência artificial, e tem acesso fácil ao presidente dos Estados Unidos.
articles.summary: Para muitos, Jensen Huang era o executivo mais poderoso do mundo. Ele liderava a empresa que controla cerca de 90% do mercado de chips avançados, usados na inteligência artificial, e tem acesso fácil ao presidente dos Estados Unidos.
articles.body:
O chefe da maior empresa de chips do mundo, a americana Nvidia , pediu demissão em meio a um escândalo de espionagem e a revelação de novos casos extraconjugais.

Para muitos, ele era o executivo mais poderoso do mundo. Liderava a empresa que controla cerca de 90% do mercado de chips avançados, usados na inteligência artificial, e com acesso fácil ao presidente dos Estados Unidos . Jensen Huang tem 63 anos, nasceu em Taiwan e cresceu nos Estados Unidos, onde adquiriu cidadania. Foi um dos fundadores da Nvidia - empresa que por anos foi conhecida por produzir placas e chips para computadores e videogames e, agora, virou peça-chave no desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial .

A imprensa americana revelou que Jensen Huang teve um caso extraconjugal com uma executiva suspeita de ser espiã da China . Alice Huang é chinesa e trabalha para a Mega Speed, uma das principais compradoras de chips da Nvidia no sudeste asiático. A empresa de Singapura aluga infraestrutura de computadores e centros de dados para companhias de outros países, como a China.

Segundo o jornal “New York Times”, os serviços de inteligência dos Estados Unidos acreditam que Alice foi recrutada por Pequim para conseguir informações sigilosas que dessem aos chineses vantagem na corrida tecnológica. Outra suspeita é de que a empresa dela teria sido usada para contrabando, para driblar restrições à venda de chips americanos para a China. As investigações também tentam esclarecer se Alice conseguiu usar a influência de Jensen Huang junto à Casa Branca para reduzir essas restrições. Donald Trump disse esta semana que conversou com o CEO e que o empresário afirmou que não tinha ideia de que Alice era uma espiã.

Chefe da Nvidia pede demissão em meio a escândalo de espionagem e a revelação de novos casos extraconjugais — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Nesta quarta-feira (11), uma outra reportagem do “New York Times” revelou que Jensen Hugan teve mais um caso extraconjugal, com uma executiva da própria Nvidia. E, nesta quinta-feira (12), a agência de notícias Reuters revelou mais um caso, com uma terceira mulher. Esta também funcionária da Nvidia. Na quarta-feira (11), a agência já tinha feito outra revelação: a de que uma universidade chinesa ligada às Forças Armadas do país conseguiu comprar chips da Nvidia em uma transação feita por uma empresa intermediária.

Logo depois da publicação, o conselho administrativo da Nvidia convocou uma reunião de emergência e nesta quinta-feira (12) cedo anunciou que Jensen Huang tinha renunciado ao cargo de CEO.

Em outubro de 2025, a Nvidia fez história ao se tornar a primeira empresa do mundo a valer mais de US$ 5 trilhões . Nunca antes uma empresa tinha valido tanto. Mas o escândalo envolvendo o CEO abalou a confiança dos investidores. Desde o fim de semana, a Nvidia perdeu mais de US$ 500 bilhões em valor de mercado. Nesta quinta-feira (12), as ações da empresa fecharam novamente em queda. Tim Oeschser, analista em mercado de capitais, afirma:

"Jensen Huang não é apenas o chefe da Nvidia, ele é o rosto da revolução da inteligência artificial. É por isso que a saída dele abalou os mercados e todos estão em alerta para o que vem pela frente”.

articles.title: Lula se reúne com rival de Trump na COP 31, na Turquia  | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente brasileiro manteve reunião privada com governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom. Democrata é um dos maiores opositores a Trump nos EUA.
articles.summary: Presidente brasileiro manteve reunião privada com governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom. Democrata é um dos maiores opositores a Trump nos EUA.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newson, durante reunião privada na COP 31, na Turquia, em 12 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/ Charles Ommanney/ gabinete do governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newson

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se reuniu nesta quinta-feira (12) com o governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom, durante a COP 31, que acontece na Turquia.

➡️ Newsom, democrata, é um dos principais opositores, dentro dos Estados Unidos, ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump . Ligado a pautas ambientais, ele costuma frequentar eventos ligados ao meio ambiente.

A equipe do governador da Califórnia afirmou que no encontro, que durou cerca de 15 minutos, Lula e Newsom falaram sobre "eleições e as mudanças climáticas, principalmente" . Foi a primeira vez que os dois se reuniram, disse ainda a equipe do californiano.

O governo brasileiro ainda não havia se pronunciado sobre o encontro até a última atualização desta reportagem.

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, ao lado do chanceler brasileiro, Mauro Vieira, conversa com o governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newson, e parte de sua equipe, na COP 31, na Turquia, em 12 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/ Charles Ommanney/ Gabinete do governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom.

No comando de um dos estados mais poderosos dos Estados Unidos, News se tornou uma das principais vozes contra Donald Trump. A rivalidade começou a ganhar notoriedade no ano passado por suas críticas e provocações a Trump.

Newsom, que está no fim de seu segundo mandato, passou a ironizar o presidente norte-americano nas redes sociais, adotando linguagem similiar à adotada pelo próprio Trump, como as letras maiúsculas e muitos pontos de interrogação, além de montagens feitas com o uso de Inteligência Artificial.

Por conta desse embate ideológico e piadas na internet contra Trump, o governador conseguiu ampliar sua projeção nacional e se tornar um dos nomes fortes do Partido Democrata.

articles.title: O que são os chips H200, no centro da polêmica que levou à renúncia do CEO da Nvidia | G1
articles.standfirst: Usado para desenvolver inteligência artificial, componentes estão sujeitos a restrições de exportação dos EUA para impedir que a China tenha acesso à tecnologia. Caso extraconjugal de Jensen Huang envolve mulher suspeita de ajudar a contrabandear os chips.
articles.summary: Usado para desenvolver inteligência artificial, componentes estão sujeitos a restrições de exportação dos EUA para impedir que a China tenha acesso à tecnologia.
articles.body:
A polêmica que levou à renúncia do CEO da Nvidia , Jensen Huang, nesta quinta-feira (12) envolve um pequeno componente: o chip H200, um dos mais avançados da empresa americana e sujeito a restrições de exportação impostas pelos Estados Unidos.

O ex-CEO da Nvidia admitiu ter traído sua esposa com a empresária chinesa Alice Huang . Autoridades americanas suspeitam que ela tenha atuado como agente de espionagem para o governo chinês e participado de operações para contrabandear chips americanos para a China.

🔎 Desde 2022, os Estados Unidos mantêm restrições de exportação para limitar o acesso da China aos chips mais avançados da Nvidia e aos equipamentos necessários para fabricá-los.

Em 2023, já sob essas restrições, a Nvidia lançou o H200 , uma evolução do H100 que oferece quase o dobro da capacidade de memória e maior velocidade de transferência de dados.

Jensen Huang, durante conferência da Nvidia em 17 de março de 2026, e GPU H200, uma das mais avançadas da empresa — Foto: Reuters/Carlos Barria; Divulgação

Os dois são GPUs (sigla em inglês para "unidades de processamento gráfico") , processadores capazes de realizar muitas operações simultaneamente e usados no treinamento de modelos de inteligência artificial e em outras aplicações que exigem alto desempenho.

Segundo a Nvidia, o H200 tem 141 gigabytes de memória de alta velocidade, contra 80 GB do H100. O modelo mais moderno alcança uma velocidade de transferência de dados de até 4,8 terabytes por segundo, enquanto seu antecessor chega a 3,35 terabytes por segundo.

A empresa afirma que o H200 usa o padrão HBM3e, uma versão aprimorada de uma tecnologia de memória que utiliza chips de memória empilhados verticalmente e posicionados próximos à GPU, o que permite transferir grandes volumes de dados em alta velocidade.

Com mais capacidade de memória e velocidade de transferência de dados, modelos de inteligência artificial, como os usados pelo ChatGPT, ficam mais rápidos para gerar respostas e pesquisadores podem executar cálculos, análises e simulações científicas de maior escala.

Empresa de Alice Huang comprou chips da Nvidia

Alice Huang, apontada como affair do então presidente-executivo da Nvidia, se apresentava como executiva da Megaspeed, uma empresa de data centers sediada em Singapura que se tornou uma das maiores clientes da Nvidia no Sudeste Asiático.

Segundo o jornal "The New York Times", a Megaspeed comprou mais de US$ 4,8 bilhões em chips da Nvidia desde junho de 2024.

A própria Megaspeed também foi alvo de investigação de autoridades americanas, sob suspeita de ter ajudado o governo chinês a obter acesso a chips avançados da Nvidia.

Em meio à polêmica, o governo dos EUA passou a ser criticado por parlamentares, que questionam a decisão do secretário de Comércio, Howard Lutnick, de não incluir mais empresas chinesas na lista de companhias sujeitas a restrições comerciais.

Lutnick é criticado por parlamentares que consideram insuficientes as medidas adotadas para restringir as exportações de chips para a China. O governo americano havia adiado em junho a inclusão de outras 100 empresas chinesas nessa lista de restrições.

Segundo a Reuters, os EUA não incluem novas empresas nessa lista desde outubro de 2025, o maior intervalo sem atualizações em mais de uma década.

Ainda segundo a agência de notícias, a decisão faria parte de uma estratégia do governo de Donald Trump para evitar o agravamento das tensões com a China.

Lutnick, com longa trajetória no mercado financeiro de Wall Street, atuou como co-presidente da equipe de transição de Trump. Amigo do presidente americano há três décadas, ele também participou, em 2008, do reality show "O Aprendiz", apresentado por Trump.

articles.title: Seca e queimadas afetam mais de 2,1 milhões de pessoas no Pará, aponta plataforma de monitoramento | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento indica que 50 municípios estão com decretos de emergência vigentes e que quase 25% do território estadual enfrenta condições de seca e fogo. Oeste do Pará e Marajó estão entre as regiões mais atingidas.
articles.summary: Levantamento indica que 50 municípios estão com decretos de emergência vigentes e que quase 25% do território estadual enfrenta condições de seca e fogo. Oeste do Pará e Marajó estão entre as regiões mais atingidas.
articles.body:
Mais de 2,1 milhões de pessoas vivem em áreas afetadas por condições de seca e fogo no Pará, segundo levantamento de uma plataforma que monitora os impactos do fenômeno El Niño. O monitoramento aponta que 50 dos 144 municípios paraenses estão com decretos de situação de emergência vigentes e que 24,9% do território estadual enfrenta condições de seca e queimadas.

Os dados são do Monitor de Antecipação e Resposta ao El Niño (MARÉ), plataforma gratuita que reúne informações oficiais sobre os efeitos do fenômeno climático. O oeste do Pará e o arquipélago do Marajó aparecem entre as regiões mais atingidas pelos incêndios florestais.

A ferramenta reúne informações sobre decretos de emergência, riscos climáticos e impactos sobre a população. O objetivo é acompanhar a situação dos municípios e subsidiar medidas de prevenção e resposta aos eventos extremos.

Os números indicam a dimensão territorial e populacional das áreas afetadas, mas não significam que todos os 2,1 milhões de moradores tenham sofrido diretamente os mesmos impactos.

Na zona rural de Monte Alegre, no oeste do Pará, moradores relatam a morte de peixes em lagos da região, em meio às altas temperaturas e à estiagem.

Em entrevista à TV Tapajós, um pescador afirmou que diferentes espécies foram encontradas mortas.

"Várias espécies de pescado, a pescada, o tucunaré e o cará... já morreram", relatou.

No arquipélago do Marajó, os incêndios florestais também têm provocado perdas materiais e dificuldades de acesso a alimentos e água para famílias de comunidades atingidas.

A situação enfrentada por moradores do Marajó e do oeste paraense foi levada à 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas (COP31), realizada na Turquia.

Representantes do Conselho Nacional das Populações Extrativistas (CNS) denunciaram os impactos das queimadas sobre as comunidades e cobraram medidas das autoridades.

"Em todos os painéis que nós estamos participando, nós estamos denunciando e pedindo ação urgente", afirmou Letícia Moraes, vice-presidente do conselho, em entrevista à TV Liberal.

Pará está sob emergência ambiental e climática

O levantamento é divulgado em meio ao agravamento da estiagem e dos incêndios florestais no estado.

Na quarta-feira (11), o Governo do Pará publicou um decreto de emergência ambiental e climática válido por 120 dias em todo o território estadual.

A medida suspende as autorizações para o uso do fogo no Pará e estabelece restrições específicas para queimadas em 31 municípios, com exceções previstas no decreto.

Os 50 municípios identificados pelo monitoramento e os 31 citados no decreto estadual representam levantamentos diferentes. O primeiro considera municípios com decretos de emergência vigentes, enquanto o segundo estabelece restrições ao uso do fogo em localidades específicas.

Segundo dados do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe) divulgados pelo g1 nesta quinta-feira (12), o Pará registrou 2.295 focos de calor nos cinco dias anteriores e liderava o ranking nacional de queimadas.

Leia também: Pará decreta emergência ambiental e climática por causa da seca

O El Niño é um fenômeno climático caracterizado pelo aquecimento anormal das águas superficiais do Oceano Pacífico Equatorial, que pode alterar os padrões de chuva e temperatura em diferentes regiões do planeta.

No Norte do Brasil, o fenômeno pode favorecer períodos de estiagem e temperaturas elevadas, aumentando as condições propícias à ocorrência de incêndios florestais.

Em agosto, o Governo do Pará já havia declarado situação de alerta climático e ambiental por 180 dias, com o objetivo de antecipar medidas diante dos impactos previstos do El Niño em 2026 e 2027.

Segundo a cientista climática Patrícia Ferrini, entrevistada pela TV Liberal, os efeitos do fenômeno devem continuar ao longo de 2027, mesmo com a previsão de pico em dezembro de 2026.

Além da seca e das queimadas, o monitoramento acompanha riscos à saúde associados aos eventos climáticos extremos, incluindo problemas respiratórios relacionados à fumaça dos incêndios e doenças que podem ser agravadas pela falta de acesso à água.

A plataforma MARÉ pode ser acessada gratuitamente pela internet, no endereço monitorelnino.com.br.

articles.standfirst: Benefício será pago em parcela única e também contempla servidores de outros órgãos cedidos ao MPRO. Pagamento depende da disponibilidade de recursos no orçamento da instituição.
articles.summary: Benefício será pago em parcela única e também contempla servidores de outros órgãos cedidos ao MPRO. Pagamento depende da disponibilidade de recursos no orçamento da instituição.
articles.body:
Servidores ativos do quadro administrativo do Ministério Público de Rondônia (MPRO) vão receber um auxílio de R$ 10 mil em dezembro de 2026. O pagamento foi autorizado por uma lei sancionada pelo governador em exercício, Alex Redano (Republicanos), e publicada nesta quinta-feira (12) no Diário Oficial do Estado de Rondônia (Diof).

➡️ De acordo com a lei, o valor tem caráter indenizatório. Isso significa que não será incorporado ao salário dos servidores nem será considerado no cálculo de vantagens pessoais ou aposentadorias.

O benefício será pago em parcela única. Também têm direito ao auxílio os servidores de outros órgãos públicos que estejam cedidos ao Ministério Público.

Por outro lado, os servidores do MPRO que estiverem cedidos a outros órgãos públicos não receberão o benefício.

O pagamento depende da disponibilidade de recursos no orçamento do próprio Ministério Público. A lei também determina que o auxílio não pode comprometer programas prioritários da instituição.

A lei entrou em vigor nesta quinta-feira (12), data da publicação.

articles.title: Operação identifica trabalhadores sem carteira assinada em galpões | G1
articles.standfirst: A operação ocorreu entre 12 e 19 de maio de 2026 em São José do Rio Preto (SP), mas as investigações foram concluídas nesta quarta-feira (11).
articles.summary: Uma operação da Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho identificou 796 trabalhadores atuando sem carteira assinada em centros de distribuição de mercadorias em São José do Rio Preto.
articles.body:
Centros de distribuição em São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

Uma operação da Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho identificou 796 trabalhadores atuando sem carteira assinada em centros de distribuição de mercadorias em São José do Rio Preto , no interior de São Paulo, e autuou em quase R$ 8 milhões tanto a plataforma de marketplace contratante do serviço quanto as empresas terceirizadas.

A operação ocorreu entre 12 e 19 de maio de 2026, mas as investigações foram concluídas nesta quarta-feira (11). Durante a fiscalização, os agentes identificaram que, entre os trabalhadores irregulares, a maioria era diaristas.

Centros de distribuição de mercadorias em São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

Uma transportadora contratada pela plataforma repassava os serviços a outras empresas, por meio das quais os trabalhadores eram selecionados. Eles eram contratados através de uma cadeia de terceirizadas para carregar, descarregas e separar mercadorias adquiridas pela população através do site da empresa de marketplace.

Ao longo das apurações, os auditores-fiscais do trabalho interditaram um galpão por risco grave de choque elétrico, de atropelamento por caminhões e de incêndio.

Ainda segundo a auditoria, mesmo após a determinação, alguns empregados foram flagrados no local, utilizando a iluminação dos celulares para exercer as atividades.

No total, foram lavrados 51 autos de infração contra oito empresas, sendo a operadora da plataforma e sete prestadoras de serviço que atuavam nos locais de fiscalização.

Ainda conforme a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho, uma parte das multas já foi quitada. As que não foram liquidadas no prazo seguiram para inscrição em Dívida Ativa da União. Em algumas situações, as empresas autuadas poderão apresentar defesa no processo administrativo.

articles.title: Car parking court case against Dudley nurse trapped in lift is dropped
articles.summary: Lisa Smith was pursued over a fine given while she was trapped in a lift when visiting a sick child.
articles.body:
Court action has been dropped against a Dudley nurse who received a parking fine after being stuck in a lift while visiting a sick child.

Community nurse Lisa Smith spent an hour and 15 minutes in a block of flats in Perry Barr Village, Birmingham, in November 2025. She parked in a permit-only bay, which medical staff are allowed to do for 30 minutes, but was trapped in a lift for more than 20 minutes before being freed by a resident.

She later received a notice that Civil Enforcement Ltd was taking her to court to recover a penalty charge of £266. Smith said she believes she is owed an apology.

The BBC has contacted Civil Enforcement Ltd for comment.

"The court sent the form back I had to complete regarding the hearing and just said it was no longer required because the case has been discontinued," said Smith.

"I would like an apology or an explanation as to why they pursued it so vigorously, even when I provided the evidence from the beginning as to why I was there and that I was stuck in a lift."

Smith's local MP, Sonia Kumar, wrote to the company, asking for the proceedings to be halted.

"Lisa was carrying out essential NHS work, caring for a vulnerable child and putting her patient's needs first," said Kumar.

"What disappointed me most was that there were multiple opportunities to bring this case to an end once the facts were clear."

Smith was not aware of the parking charge straight away because she was driving an NHS pool car and was later off work due to illness.

She said she was now free from the worry of facing court action and said people in a similar situation should dispute claims against them.

This news was gathered by the Local Democracy Reporting Service which covers councils and other public service organisations.

articles.title: Single and trying to find love? Be sure you're not 'floodlighting'
articles.summary: Single? Watch out for "floodlighting," when sharing too much, too soon creates the illusion of intimacy.
articles.body:
Have you ever told a first date more about your toxic ex than they probably wanted to know?

You may be floodlighting. It's a dating trend when someone shares too much, too soon in a romantic setting, falsely creating the illusion of intimacy with a partner.

The term was coined by Brené Brown , author of "The Power of Vulnerability: Teachings of Authenticity, Connections and Courage," who explains it as when a switch is turned on and all the light blasts through at full intensity instead of slowly letting light in.

Amy Chan , a dating coach and author of " UNSINGLE: How to Date Smarter and Create Love That Lasts ," notes that daters sometimes floodlight because they're afraid they'll get rejected if they share their trauma later in a relationship.

"In anticipation of that potential future rejection, they want to lay it all out on the table, and see if someone is willing to stay," Chan says.

Another reason can be wanting validation.

"Someone might share their hardships and how terrible the past few relationships were so they can get sympathy, and maybe even trauma bond ," Chan says.

Philip Lewis , a Beverly Hills-based relationship therapist, says adults who didn't feel heard or understood as children can develop a habit of oversharing in an unconscious effort to make sure they receive that as an adult.

"Some overshare in a misbelief that it shows a certain vulnerability that might attract someone. In reality, oversharing isn't relational, and is more likely to push your date away than draw them in," Lewis says.

Lewis says he sometimes sees oversharing used as a "stress test," where someone feeling insecure about themselves or their past shares about it early on, thinking, "If you can handle this, maybe we have a future."

This is often due to a fear of rejection and can backfire.

"Most listeners will feel uncomfortable, not sympathetic, and that's a turn-off," Lewis says. "Rather than building intimacy, oversharing signals a lack of healthy boundaries."

Chan and Lewis say that if your date or partner is floodlighting, you don't need to play therapist or overshare to match their emotional intensity.

Instead, give them the benefit of the doubt and steer the conversation somewhere lighter.

"You could say something like, 'I'm having a little trouble contributing to our conversations. I'd like to tell you more about myself. Would you be open to making room for that?' or, 'I'm sorry to hear what happened to you in the past. I'm curious how you're coping with that today,'" Lewis says.

If you find yourself oversharing, take a breath and try to identify where the urge is coming from. Ultimately, if you like each other, there will be plenty of time to build deeper intimacy in the future.

"Notice the urge and ask yourself what you're hoping to get from sharing," Lewis says. "If you've already overshared, name it and make room for your date to open up: 'I think I shared a lot, fast. I'd like to hear more about you.'"

articles.title: Bigger than the Titanic, this historic ship is now a giant reef
articles.summary: The nearly 1,000-foot ship took just hours to descend to the ocean floor near Destin-Fort Walton Beach, becoming the world’s largest artificial reef.
articles.body:
Weather conditions accelerated the final voyage of the SS United States, with crews sinking the historic ocean liner off Florida 's Panhandle on Wednesday, a day earlier than planned.

The nearly 1,000-foot ship, larger than the Titanic, took just hours to descend to the ocean floor near Destin -Fort Walton Beach, becoming the world's largest artificial reef.

The sinking had been scheduled for Thursday, but weather conditions prompted crews to move the operation forward. The ship now rests in the Gulf about 25 miles southwest of Destin.

Just days before the sinking, a Florida federal judge dismissed a lawsuit challenging the project. The lawsuit argued that federal regulators had failed to adequately review potential environmental impacts and historic preservation concerns before granting approval.

The decision cleared a major obstacle to the ship's transformation from a celebrated passenger liner into an underwater destination.

Once a symbol of American engineering and luxury, the SS United States carried presidents and celebrities across the Atlantic. In 1952, it set the transatlantic speed record for passenger ships, a distinction it still holds more than 70 years later.

But after decades out of service, the vessel faced an uncertain future, including the possibility of being scrapped.

Okaloosa County purchased the ship with plans to sink it and create an artificial reef, giving the aging liner a new role off the Florida coast.

Over time, the vessel is expected to provide habitat for fish and other marine life while attracting scuba divers interested in exploring the historic ship.

articles.title: Sheinbaum rebuts Trump, says no migrant caravans have reached US border since January 2025
articles.summary: MEXICO CITY (AP) — Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Thursday that no migrant caravans have reached the U. President Donald Trump returned to office i...
articles.body:
MEXICO CITY (AP) — Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Thursday that no migrant caravans have reached the U.S. border since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025, responding to his threat to double tariffs on Mexican goods unless Mexico stops migrants from traveling through its territory.

"Not a single migrant caravan has reached the north" since January 2025, Sheinbaum said at her daily news briefing.

Sheinbaum said a caravan of about 600 migrants traveling through the southern state of Chiapas had largely dispersed after its members were told that reaching the United States would be "very difficult."

She said Mexican authorities were also in talks with another group of several hundred Honduran migrants, encouraging them to return to their home country.

Asked whether Mexico would use force to break up the caravans, Sheinbaum ruled out such measures, saying authorities have "extensive experience" accompanying migrants and explaining that they have little chance of crossing into the United States.

Earlier Thursday, Trump claimed on Truth Social that the United States faced an "invasion" following midterm elections in which Democrats won control of Congress.

"Huge caravans are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico. Many of the people in these Caravans are those that various countries don't want," he wrote. "MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED."

Following the election, Trump named Stephen Miller , an architect of his hard-line immigration policies, as White House chief of staff.

Trump's latest tariff threat comes as Mexico and the United States continue negotiations aimed at reducing or eliminating duties Washington imposed on several Mexican products last year.

The talks coincide with a review of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement , or USMCA, which began in July.

Mexico is seeking significant reductions in the 10% tariffs imposed on Mexican goods not covered by the trade agreement, as well as the 25% duty on medium- and heavy-duty trucks.

Negotiations have also addressed a 50% tariff on steel and aluminum and a 17% countervailing duty on Mexican tomatoes.

articles.title: Wangchuk under ‘house arrest’ as Ladakh rallies against hill council polls in winter
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was put under “house arrest” Thursday as an agitation began against a govt
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was put under “house arrest” Thursday as an agitation began against a govt decision to hold Ladakh hill council polls on Dec 4 despite pleas to avoid the elections in the Union Territory (UT) during the harsh winter.Police removed Wangchuk from protest site NDS Memorial Park in Leh late Wednesday when he went there to oversee preparations, initially saying he “has been advised to stay at his residence”. Later, the Leh SSP issued formal “preventive” orders and restrictions on Wangchuk, saying his “activities, antecedents and alleged attempts to instigate the general public have affected public order before and there is an apprehension his future demonstrations may again lead to disturbance of peace”. “Dozens of armed guards surround my house,” Wangchuk posted late Thursday.A ban was clamped Wednesday on protests in view of the Dec 4 hill council polls and municipal/panchayat polls on Nov 21.Wangchuk and his LAB colleagues then issued an “SOS” appeal to President Droupadi Murmu, PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah to defer the polls. They cited the harsh winter and likely exclusion of many voters. LAB co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook has said nearly 30% of the population is outside the region during winter.On Thursday, LAB said despite the crackdown and heavy deployment of security in Leh and Kargil, people from all walks of life participated in a peaceful dharna. “It sends a clear message to the administration that the people of Ladakh believe in peaceful and democratic means of protest and remain determined to raise their legitimate demands while exercising their constitutional right to protest, as guaranteed by the Constitution,” LAB said in a statement.Speaking at the protest site, Lakrook argued that LAB was not opposed to the hill council polls but holding them in winter would deprive a large number of people from voting. He also alleged that electoral rolls have been tampered with and Gen Z voters removed, calling it “Operation Lotus”.The elections follow an Oct 20 notification paving the way for hill councils in all eight districts in Ladakh, including newly created Sankoo. Ladakh earlier had two hill councils, one each in Leh and Kargil.Chief secretary Ashish Kundra has described the hill council polls as a “watershed moment” for Ladakh’s democracy. He has argued that schools remain open in the region till Dec 15 and if children can attend classes, there is no no reason adults can’t turn out to vote. articles.title: Did Ro Khanna and his wife sell NVIDIA shares just before the spy scandal involving Jensen Huang broke out?

articles.body: Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna, who has advocated banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks, and his wife sold Nvidia shares around the time the chipmaker's stock reached record highs, according to financial disclosures tracked by Capitol Trades. This led to online speculation as to whether he had any information about Nvidia former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang, allegedly a spy. Khanna is dead against Congress members trading stock and hence the rumors are flying high. But these are only rumors and online speculation.Khanna's wife made two Nvidia stock sales, each valued between $1,000 and $15,000, on September 4 and October 7, according to the disclosures. Nvidia shares reached an all-time high on October 6, just a day before the second reported sale.The transactions came ahead of a sharp decline in Nvidia's share price this week after Huang's affairs were revealed.Khanna represents California's 17th Congressional District and has been among the lawmakers calling for restrictions on stock trading by members of Congress. He also serves on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.The latest transactions were not the first time Khanna and his wife had sold Nvidia shares around a stock-price high. According to Capitol Trades, Khanna sold two lots of Nvidia stock, each valued between $1,000 and $15,000, in early and late May. Nvidia shares reached their second-highest level on May 14.However, the disclosures also show that Khanna acquired Nvidia shares between June and September.What is the Nvidia controversy?Huang had to resign in the wake of the major scandal that unfolded after his relationship with Alice Huang was reported. He told President Donald Trump that he was not aware of the allegations against Alice.Nvidia shares fell 7% during the week through Wednesday's close and dropped another 8% in overnight trading following reports speculating about a second alleged affair involving Huang and the possibility of his departure.Khanna's position on congressional stock tradingKhanna has previously called for banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks, arguing for restrictions on lawmakers' ability to profit from investments while serving in public office.The issue has faced renewed scrutiny in Washington. The House passed the Stop Insider Trading Act in July 2026, which would prohibit lawmakers, their spouses and dependent children from purchasing individual stocks. articles.summary: Twitch streamer Ludwig Ahgren has hit back at players who questioned his gaming skills after he struggled with Deadlock.
articles.body: Twitch streamer Ludwig Ahgren has hit back at players who questioned his gaming skills after he struggled with Deadlock. The streamer lost his patience with the game's buy menu during a November 10, 2026, livestream. His complaints soon became a topic of discussion among players. However, when one X user used his gameplay to question his intelligence, Ahgren had a sharp response. He argued that learning Deadlock has little to do with intelligence and is mostly about spending time with the game.Ludwig Ahgren Compares Deadlock's Buy Menu to the Disneyland App During His LivestreamAhgren was playing Deadlock with fellow streamers SuperTF, Squeex, Valkyrae, and TinaKitten when he became frustrated with the game's shopping system. He had 3,000 souls available but could not figure out what items he could purchase.The situation quickly tested his patience. He openly complained about the interface and questioned why Valve had designed the buy menu that way."I don't understand anything! I don't understand anything! Who the **** thought this buy menu made any god**** sense?! It looks like the Disneyland app. **** this ****, man... I have 3,000 souls; I don't even know what I can **ing buy!.. Dumb game, bro."His reaction was part of the November 10 broadcast, which also featured other gaming and entertainment segments. The stream archive lists the broadcast under the title "HUGE NEWS➡️TRIVIA➡️REACTS➡️DEADLOCK WITH friends :)."StreamRecorder+1However, the argument did not end with his complaints about the menu. The following day, Ahgren returned to the clip while reviewing reactions to his gameplay.An X user named @lesserthantwink had reposted his frustrated reaction and wrote, "This game is a really good filter for dumb****es [low-key]."The comment suggested that players who struggle with Deadlock lack the intelligence needed to understand it. Ahgren clearly disagreed and decided to address the criticism himself.Ludwig Ahgren Calls Out Deadlock Players and Compares Their Attitude to Rick and Morty FansAhgren was not happy with people treating knowledge of Deadlock as proof of higher intelligence. He said the game does not require any special level of intelligence. According to him, players simply need time to understand its systems.He also mocked the idea that knowing how to play a particular game makes someone smarter than others."Oh, people gotta stop stroking their ***** proudly on Twitter. It's embarrassing. 'This game is a good filter for dumb****es.' (Sarcastically) 'Oh, yeah, man. The real test of intelligence. I studied the Deadlock buy menu.' What are we doing here? What are we talking about? 'Check my IQ tests. I'm ****ing silver in Deadlock.' Please be serious for a moment. All it is is a mild learning gap. That's all it is. There's no intelligence required. It's just a time angle."He then brought up League of Legends and chess to explain his point. Ahgren questioned whether players should be considered intelligent simply because they understand certain game mechanics or chess openings."You think a League of Legends player is smart because they know how to buy Tabis? You think a chess player is smart because they know the Catalan opening and the response? Chess players are ****ing idiots. So are Deadlock players. So are League players. And we're all just trying to find our little thing we can get addicted to, to move on with the rest of our lives until we die. That's it. Everyone's a ****ing idiot."The streamer also compared the people defending Deadlock's difficulty to fans of Rick and Morty. He mocked their claims that the game demands more intelligence than other titles."It sounds like Rick and Morty fans... It's pathetic. (Mockingly) 'Actually, Deadlock requires a higher level of intellect to play than other games.' Please! Pathetic!"Rather than accepting the criticism, Ahgren stood by his view that understanding a game's menu and mechanics comes with practice. His response focused on the difference between learning a game and being naturally intelligent.He later explained why he thought the criticism was unfair online that day.You use AI every day. articles.title: 2 SPOs killed in J&K’s Kishtwar, service rifles missing
articles.summary: JAMMU/SRINAGAR: Bullet-riddled bodies of two special police officers (SPOs) were found in the remote forests of J&K’s Kishtwar district Thursday, with
articles.body: JAMMU/SRINAGAR: Bullet-riddled bodies of two special police officers (SPOs) were found in the remote forests of J&K’s Kishtwar district Thursday, with their service rifles missing, triggering a search for the attackers and renewed concerns over a possible revival of terrorism in Chenab valley.Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57, both residents of Kiyar Dachhan and posted with SOG Kiyar sector, had gone missing on Nov 10 while travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah for rotation duty. A search was launched after they failed to reach the post. Their mobile phones were initially reachable but later switched off.One SPO had a bullet wound to his head and the other to his back. Their bodies were shifted for autopsy. Their INSAS and .303 rifles were missing.Sources said it was too early to link the killings to terrorism. However, Hizbul Mujahideen commander Jahangir Saroori, believed to be the longest-surviving terrorist in Chenab valley, was suspected to have been hiding in the area for decades. Mudassar, Riaj and south Kashmir terrorist Latif Bhat were also trying to revive terrorism in the region, the sources added.The killings came as security forces intensified searches in south Kashmir’s Kulgam after a terrorist fired at a CRPF checkpoint around 70km south of Srinagar Wednesday, wounding three personnel. A CRPF officer said the attack appeared to have been carried out by a lone gunman using a high-calibre weapon, possibly an AK-47, before escaping. The wounded men were out of danger.Political parties condemned both the Kulgam attack and the Kishtwar killings. J&K leader of opposition Sunil Sharma alleged terrorists had kidnapped the SPOs while they were travelling through the dense forest. “These terrorists, who are on the verge of being wiped out, are still trying to make their presence felt. This is a matter of concern for us,” he said.Former NC MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi said the attacks were intended to derail the progress towards peace. “The perpetrators must be held accountable without delay,” he said.SPOs are temporary, honorarium-based local recruits appointed to assist J&K police. Trained in handling weapons, they support village defence committees, and participate in counter-terrorism operations alongside security forces in remote areas.In a separate operation in north Kashmir, security forces rounded up Ghulam Jeelani Reshi of Tangmarg from a forest. One hand grenade was found on him and another was found concealed in the forest following his disclosure, police said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Who was Matt Lambert? DC gym shooter was a wealthy doctor who was fighting with the management of his $1.1M penthouse over black mold
articles.summary: The DC shooter who opened fire at his apartment gym and them shot himself was not a deranged migrant but a wealthy emergency room doctor.
articles.body: The DC shooter who opened fire at his apartment gym and them shot himself was not a deranged migrant but a wealthy emergency room doctor. According to reports, Dr Matt Lambert has been posting on social media on the infestation of black mold in his $1.1 million painthouse and his "manifesto" posted shortly before he opened fire was also about a suspected microbial growth.“My manifesto is an engineering report,” an X account linked to Lambert tweeted Thursday morning. The X account (ofmiceand mold) was full of his posts on molds and other grievances related to his apartment.Last year, Lambert had sued Metropole Condominium Association aleeging that repairs to the building led to mold festering in his home as the building was scaffolded.“Two years of living in luxury (and the start of 6 months with no shower, dryer, HVAC, and cooking),” an X account linked to Lambert posted Wednesday, along with pictures showing renovations in the Logan Circle unit.New York Post reported that Dr Lambert lived on the 7th floor of 1515 15th St NW. On Wednesday morning, he opened fire at the ground-floor gym killing at least one person. Then he ran back up to his apartment where he remained in hiding or nearly an hour before he killed himself.Lambert described himself as “a board-certified emergency physician with over two decades of clinical experience” and a medical tech executive on his personal website. “He has a deep understanding of healthcare regulations and their impact on technology adoption,” the site said."Beyond his professional pursuits, Dr. Lambert is a published author, musician, and a dedicated philanthropist. He has volunteered his medical expertise in underserved communities, including Kenya, Belize, and Haiti. Dr. Lambert splits his time between the mountains of West Virginia and the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, DC," it read.Ward 2 Council Member Brooke Pinto, who represents and lives in the area, said preliminary information suggests the shooter was targeting someone in Vida Fitness and “that he had been in active litigation with over a condo issue.” It’s just so sad and so senseless to kill someone over a dispute that should be worked out reasonably,” she told NBC News.Mold toxicity: Major debate on social mediaAfter his social media account was revealed, a major debate started on X as people commented to his manifesto that 'black mold' can not be the reason to open fire and kill people. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid continuing incidents of violence in ethnic-strife-hit Manipur, govt sources Thursday expressed confidence that the assembly polls in the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid continuing incidents of violence in ethnic-strife-hit Manipur, govt sources Thursday expressed confidence that the assembly polls in the state will be held on schedule.The term of the Manipur assembly ends on March 13 next year, and the state is due to go to the polls alongside Goa, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh.However, a long phase of ethnic violence, which has subsided but continues to persist sporadically, has left political circles wondering if the Manipur polls will be held on time."It will be held on time," a source said when asked.EC, which has been making preparations, put Manipur's electorate at 19.94 lakh in its draft rolls, signalling an expansion of the voter base by nearly 2% before assembly elections expected by March. The draft rolls, prepared after a special summary revision (SSR), added 33,737 electors to the rolls published following Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Sept.The 60 assembly constituencies of the state registered a rise in voter numbers, with women outnumbering men by 55,437. Saikot recorded the highest gain of more than 2,600 electors.The window for filing claims and objections will remain open until Dec 11. articles.title: 5 people found alive after 3 months adrift at sea in tiny 20-foot boat
articles.summary: After drifting for three months across the Pacific Ocean from Micronesia, five survivors, including two children, were found off Fanning Island in Kiribati.
articles.body: Five people, including two children, have been rescued in the remote Pacific Ocean after surviving for three months adrift in a small boat, according to authorities and international news outlets. The three adults and two children who were rescued on Nov. 1 were among nine passengers who set out July 30. Their trip was intended to be a routine, one-hour crossing between the Micronesian islands of Murilo and Ruo, according to reports from the Australian Broadcasting Corp. (ABC) and The Times of London. Shortly after departure, however, a sudden storm pushed the 20-foot skiff off course, leaving it stranded in open waters. CRUISE SHIP BATTLES ROUGH PACIFIC SEAS TO SAVE INJURED, STRANDED SAILOR After the disappearance, the U.S. Coast Guard launched an extensive search operation across the region. After scouring over 25,000 nautical miles across 31 search patterns without locating the vessel, the agency suspended its active search on Aug. 10, it said in an initial news release. The ordeal ended when residents of Fanning Island in Kiribati spotted the vessel drifting off their coast and brought the five passengers ashore, according to the ABC and The Times. Kiribati lawmaker Kaotitaake Rakoroa told news outlets the survivors were taken in by a local church pastor, who provided immediate shelter and care. ‘Thanks be to God’ The five were suffering from severe malnutrition and dehydration upon arrival. Despite their physical condition, local medical staff noted steady improvement. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Paukin Tororo, a nursing officer treating the survivors, told the ABC that the group had started showing positive signs of recovery, including smiling, moving their heads and indicating an appetite for food. Authorities have not released details on how the group survived the three-month journey or what happened to the four passengers who remain unaccounted for to this day. "Incredible and wonderful news. These five folks were found and are receiving care," the U.S. Coast Guard told The Associated Press (AP) in an email. "We continue to pray for their four companions." "Our profound condolences to family and friends of those who did not arrive with them." When asked by the AP what happened to the missing four, the Coast Guard said it was continuing to gather and confirm information and would reply as soon as possible. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES Alexander Narruhn, governor of Micronesia’s Chuuk state, has started discussions with the Kiribati government to arrange repatriation for the survivors, the AP said. "There were nine people aboard the boat that went missing. Thanks be to God for his love and mercy that five of the nine have been found," Narruhn said through an interpreter in a statement cited by the AP. "We continue to pray for their four companions." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The members of the group have yet to speak publicly about their ordeal and have asked for their privacy to be respected. Family members in the Federated States of Micronesia told media outlets they have been in contact with some of the group. articles.title: Actor Ian Ziering, known for Beverly Hills, 90210, was promised $200,000 in unpaid hosting fees secured against three sports cars; he claims the vehicles were not even owned by the production company
articles.summary: Actor Ian Ziering, best known for his role in Beverly Hills, 90210, has filed a lawsuit claiming he is owed $200,000 in unpaid hosting fees for The CW's
articles.body: Actor Ian Ziering, best known for his role in Beverly Hills, 90210, has filed a lawsuit claiming he is owed $200,000 in unpaid hosting fees for The CW's The Great American Road Rally. According to the New York Post, the actor initially received $60,000 of his promised $260,000 salary, with the remaining amount scheduled in two instalments. The dispute also involves three sports cars listed as collateral for the unpaid fees. However, Ziering alleges that the vehicles, a Ford F-150 Shelby Super Snake, Dodge Challenger and Chevrolet Corvette Z51, were not owned by the production company named in his agreement.Why is actor Ian Ziering claiming $200,000 in unpaid hosting feesAccording to the lawsuit, Ziering began hosting The Great American Road Rally in September 2025. The programme features celebrities navigating 2,211 miles of cross-country terrain along Route 66. His reported hosting salary was $260,000, of which he initially received $60,000. The remaining amount was scheduled to be paid in two instalments of $100,000 each.The payments were due on August 23 and October 21, 2026. However, the lawsuit alleges that the defendants failed to make the second payment. The legal filing states that the defendants "failed and refused to pay the 100,000 instalment due October 21". The lawsuit does not specify whether Ziering received the first instalment scheduled for August.How did Ziering's hosting contract describe the deferred compensation arrangementThe hosting contract reportedly included a clause identifying three vehicles as collateral for the deferred compensation. According to the lawsuit, the arrangement was made because Ziering was agreeing to provide professional services while postponing a substantial portion of his payment. The legal papers described this as an agreement to furnish "valuable professional services while deferring substantial compensation".The three vehicles listed in the filing were a 2016 F-150 Shelby Super Snake, a 2014 Dodge Challenger and a 2023 Chevrolet Corvette Z51. According to the New York Post, the vehicles had a combined stated value of $200,000 or more. They were identified in the agreement as security for the unpaid hosting fees.Who owns the three sports cars listed as collateral in Ian Ziering's lawsuitA key issue raised in the lawsuit concerns the ownership of the three cars. Ziering alleges that the vehicles were not owned by The Great American Road Rally LLC, but instead belonged to production company 7BMG. The production company and its chief executive, Eric Richey, are also named as defendants in the lawsuit.The actor further claims that the vehicles have not been made available to him. The ownership dispute is central to the agreement because the cars were reportedly identified as collateral for the deferred compensation. The lawsuit therefore raises questions about the vehicles' ownership and whether the arrangement provided the security described in the contract.How much compensation is Ziering seeking in his lawsuit over unpaid hosting feesAccording to the New York Post, Ziering is seeking $100,000 plus interest in connection with the unpaid compensation. The lawsuit also details the work he says he completed for the programme, including preproduction activities and filming in the City of Santa Monica, at a car dealership and at a desert location in California.The defendants were contacted for comment, according to the report. Meanwhile, The Great American Road Rally features celebrities travelling along the famous Route 66 for various charitable causes. The programme's next episode was scheduled to air on The CW on November 11, 2026. The allegations of unpaid fees and the three vehicles are part of a lawsuit filed by Ziering.Disclaimer: This article is based on information publicly available, including reports by the New York Post and allegations made in the lawsuit filed by Ian Ziering. The Times of India has not independently verified the claims concerning the unpaid hosting fees, ownership of the three vehicles or the terms of the compensation agreement. The allegations should not be interpreted as facts, and the defendants' responses, if any, have not been independently verified.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: What happened at Ole Miss? Viral video shows students making monkey noises and gestures outside Black students' apartment. Donors raise money for accused Lauren Mayfield
articles.summary: A viral video from the University of Mississippi, commonly known as Ole Miss, has sparked a racism controversy after two white female students were caught
articles.body: A viral video from the University of Mississippi, commonly known as Ole Miss, has sparked a racism controversy after two white female students were caught on a doorbell camera making monkey-like noises and gestures outside an apartment occupied by Black students. The incident has triggered a university investigation, public apologies and calls for disciplinary action.The controversy began on November 6, when a ring doorbell camera outside an apartment in Oxford, Mississippi, recorded three white women walking past the entrance. Two of them appeared to beat their chests and make monkey-like noises and gestures while looking towards the camera.The footage was shared on TikTok by Jakiyra Metcalf, a Black freshman at Ole Miss who lives in the apartment with two other Black students, Victoria Johnson and Kaiyden Caldwell. The 13-second clip quickly went viral, attracting more than 13 million views and widespread criticism.What happened after the video was recorded?Metcalf and her roommates said they went outside to confront the women after watching the footage.According to the students, one of the women, identified as 18-year-old Alaina Kunes, apologized. She reportedly explained that the women had been making similar noises and gestures outside other apartment doors.However, the roommates said the second woman (Lauren Mayfield) continued making the gestures even as Kunes already said sorry"She continued to make the gestures after the girl was apologizing," Johnson told CBS News. "It was like a slap in the face."The students said the behaviour was hurtful regardless of whether the women knew they were Black.What did the student accused of making the gestures say?Kunes issued a public apology on November 10 through a statement released by her representative."To the women I offended and to the Ole Miss community, I sincerely apologize," she said.Kunes claimed she had never met the women involved before November 6 and was unaware of their race. She acknowledged that her actions were insensitive, inappropriate and deeply harmful."I would have never intentionally made those noises or gestures toward a person of color," she said.She also said she had apologized directly to the women and intended to cooperate fully with the university's investigation.Kunes voluntarily withdrew from the university.What has Ole Miss said?The University of Mississippi condemned the behaviour and launched an investigation through its Office of Conflict Resolution and Student Conduct and Equal Opportunity and Regulatory Compliance.Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs Shawnboda Mead described the behaviour as deeply troubling, hurtful and unacceptable.The university said it had contacted the students affected by the incident to offer support and connect them with available resources.Officials also cautioned against spreading unverified information, saying at least one student had been wrongly identified online. The university said no members of its sorority community were involved.Why has the incident attracted so much attention?The controversy has revived discussions about the University of Mississippi's history of racial discrimination.Ole Miss was at the centre of a major civil rights confrontation in 1962 when James Meredith became its first Black student. His admission triggered violent riots after Mississippi authorities and segregationists attempted to prevent him from enrolling.The latest incident has prompted Black students and their parents to question whether the university is doing enough to ensure that students from different racial backgrounds feel safe and welcome.Demetrick Stringer Jr., president of the university's Black Student Union, called for accountability, support for the affected students and stronger efforts to educate newcomers about the university's commitment to respecting every individual.The three students targeted in the latest incident have said they intend to remain at Ole Miss.Viral fundraiser for Lauren MayfieldThe incident took a new turn with a fundraiser for Lauren Mayfield going viral. Lauren is not one of the victims but she is the woman who did not apologize and many on Internet think she is right. And that's why a fundraiser for her on Givesendgo is going viral. "She did nothing wrong. She did not assault anyone. She did not break any law. She made noises in a public walkway. The rest is a campus bureaucracy and online mob treating a juvenile stunt as a hate crime because the residents were black. The same institutions that excuse actual violence, riots, and anti-White rhetoric when the identities flip are now treating this as grounds for expulsion, doxxing, death threats, and career destruction," the fundraiser said.You use AI every day. articles.title: ICE Says It's Deporting More Immigrants Than Ever. Many Are Actually Leaving Voluntarily.
articles.summary: Immigrants facing poorly vetted agents and a lack of due process are choosing to leave the country on their own terms.
articles.body:
On Thursday, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced that in FY 2026, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) "broke the record for the highest number of deportations and arrests in any fiscal year," with "more than 491,000 immigration arrests and more than 483,000 deportations."

ICE claimed that its numbers in FY 2026 alone "dwarfed deportation and arrest numbers from the entirety of the Biden Administration." Indeed, internal ICE data—obtained through the Freedom of Information Act by the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse (TRAC), a nonpartisan data research organization— show that in FY 2026, ICE recorded the highest number of deportations since FY 2009. That year, under President Barack Obama, ICE deported 489,251 people.

In a statement, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin credited President Donald Trump's "leadership" for unleashing the agency to "target and remove illegal aliens." However, the agency's data show that it has carried out fewer removal operations under the Trump administration than in previous years. ICE can conduct fewer operations while keeping its deportation numbers high because immigrants are increasingly choosing to self-deport or turn back at the border.

In July and August, voluntary departures and voluntary returns—deportation processes that allow illegal immigrants to depart the U.S. of their own volition with no removal order or "related immigration consequences"—made up 37 percent of total deportations, compared with the first three months of the Trump administration, when they accounted for "less than 5 percent." In FY 2026, immigration judges issued 11 times as many orders for voluntary departures as in FY 2024.

ICE's deportation totals—which include methods such as voluntary departures, withdrawals of applications for admission, and voluntary returns that allow reentry into the country—are typically grouped under deportations. The all-inclusive figure might play well to the president's supporters, but it obscures the atmosphere of fear and illiberalism powering the Trump administration's deportation numbers.

ICE set a goal to hire 10,000 new officers and agents within a year. To meet its goal, the agency has lowered hiring standards, sending prospective officers out to enforce Trump's immigration agenda with little training, often before their background checks are even complete. On Tuesday, The Washington Post reported that a review of a "small fraction" of the 12,000 recent hires by DHS found "at least 19 officers who had faced past allegations of misconduct or criminal charges, or had other employment red flags," including at least six cases in which officers were "fired or decertified, or resigned under threat of dismissal."

On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that David Brouillette—the rookie ICE officer who fatally shot a Colombian immigrant in Maine in July—had a "record of deep-seated anti-immigrant hostility, especially against Colombians." Despite the documented claims against Brouillette, he was "fast-tracked through a preliminary vetting process" and "allowed to skip ICE's full training course in Georgia." The Times reported that "at the time of the shooting in Maine," ICE hadn't reviewed Brouillette's background report, so it had no indication whether he had red flags that would make him undesirable as a law enforcement officer.

Being shot or beaten by unaccountable federal officers is one thing. Immigrants must also account for the possibility that they could be deported to a third country or secretly transferred out of state without notice to their loved ones or legal counsel.

In a choice between state-sanctioned violence and a peaceful return on their own terms, it's hardly surprising that immigrants would choose to depart the U.S. voluntarily rather than risk becoming another victim of the Trump administration's policies.

Exit polls from NBC News and CNN show that Trump's immigration enforcement tactics were unpopular with midterm voters. Yet the president seems ready to double down on his policies. After floating the possibility of working out an amnesty deal with the incoming Democratic-led Congress, Trump told reporters Wednesday that there'd be "no amnesty," and that he hadn't "told Stephen Miller," the mastermind behind his immigration agenda and the new White House chief of staff, to "make any changes to the administration's efforts to deport millions."

Outside of partisan bluster, Democrats have shown little evidence they can act as a bulwark against the Trump administration's immigration enforcement agenda. Trump could veto any bill passed by a Democratic-led Congress, and two years of a Republican majority have left ICE fully funded with over $152 billion in taxpayer money unspent between it and Customs and Border Protection.

Still, the incoming Congress could exercise its authority over appropriations and rescind the funds bankrolling ICE's campaign of intimidation.
